task.title: Remove rubber-stamp Q&A questions from festina-scope and festina-create
task.description: Remove ~6 rubber-stamp AskUserQuestion calls from festina-scope (dependencies, patterns, constraints) and festina-create (priority, label confirmation, engineering doc type). Replace with auto-inferred decisions that are stated as output, not asked as questions. Users can still volunteer overrides during Q&A. Continues the "propose, don't interrogate" principle established in task #016.
task.problem: festina-scope asks 3 questions during technical Q&A that users always answer with the default: "Are there any libraries or dependencies?" (always "None"), "Should we follow these patterns?" (always "Yes"), "Are there any technical constraints?" (always "None"). festina-create asks for priority confirmation (always "Medium"), label confirmation when auto-detected (always "Yes"), and engineering doc type when no docs match (always "None needed"). These violate the "propose, don't interrogate" principle already stated in the scope skill source (lines 582-585) and partially applied in task #016 which removed 14 similar confirmations.
task.value: Fewer interruptions per skill invocation (~6 questions removed), faster workflow through the two most-used skills, and consistent application of the "propose, don't interrogate" principle. The same treatment that task #016 applied to boundaries, research depth, and synthesis approval now extends to the remaining rubber-stamp questions.
task.acceptance-criteria:
Given festina-scope reaches the technical Q&A phase (conduct_qa_dialogue step) Then the dependencies question (line 620-628) is removed — dependencies are inferred from research findings and stated as decisions And the patterns question (line 630-639) is removed — found patterns are auto-included with a statement, not a confirmation And the constraints question (line 641-649) is removed — constraints from pitfalls/research are stated as decisions And users can still volunteer dependencies/patterns/constraints at any point during Q&A
Given festina-create detects a label from keywords Then the label is auto-applied without confirmation — output the decision as a statement And only ask when label detection fails (no keywords match)
Given festina-create reaches priority selection Then priority defaults to "medium" without asking — output the decision as a statement
Given festina-create finds no matching engineering docs (score < 0.3) Then engineering doc type is set to "none" without asking — stub creation deferred to festina-finalize if needed
Given a user wants to override any auto-decision Then they can volunteer corrections during Q&A (e.g., "actually use high priority", "we need library X", "don't follow that pattern") And the skill incorporates the override into the final output
task.notes:
**Research references:** - Research: Full inventory of ~150-180 AskUserQuestion calls across all skills performed during discovery - Research: Task #016 removed 14 confirmations using "show work, don't ask permission" principle — this task extends that work - Research: festina-scope lines 582-585 state "Propose, don't interrogate" but only 2 of 5 Q&A questions follow it (approach and files propose; dependencies, patterns, constraints don't) - Research: Boundaries question was already made voluntary in #016 (line 651) — dependencies and constraints should get the same treatment
**Integration points:** - Continues work started in task #016 (remove unnecessary user confirmations) - Skills affected: festina-scope (SKILL.md lines 620-649), festina-create (SKILL.md priority/label/eng-type steps) - Both skills are Handlebars templates in apps/festinalente/src/content/skills/
**Design principles:** - User: "I literally ALWAYS just spam yes on" these questions — they add friction without value - Inferred: Auto-decisions should be stated as output (e.g., "Priority: medium. Label: refactor.") so the user sees what was decided and can object - Inferred: The "volunteer during Q&A" escape hatch preserves user agency without forcing confirmation on every decision
